question.title: Will a fault-tolerant quantum computer be available to commercial users before January 1, 2030?
question.description:
*This forecasting question is associated with the Verity controversy:* [*Will a fault-tolerant quantum computer be available to commercial users before January 1, 2030?*](https://www.verity.news/controversy/will-a-fault-tolerant-quantum-computer-be-available-to-commercial-users-before-january-1-2030)

[Quantum computers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_computing) use the principles of [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics) to solve certain problems that are difficult or impractical for classical computers. Most current systems are considered **noisy** [**intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noisy_intermediate-scale_quantum_computing), meaning they are prone to errors and cannot reliably perform long, complex computations. A [**fault-tolerant quantum computer**](https://www.ibm.com/quantum/blog/what-is-ftqc) uses quantum error correction to protect information from these errors, making large-scale, reliable quantum computation possible. The [U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)](https://www.nist.gov/) identifies fault tolerance as a key milestone toward practical quantum computing.

Several companies—including [IBM](https://www.ibm.com/quantum/blog/large-scale-ftqc), [Google](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/research/quantum-hardware-verifiable-advantage/), [Microsoft](https://quantum.microsoft.com/en-us/vision/quantum-roadmap), [Quantinuum](https://www.quantinuum.com/blog/quantinuum-overcomes-last-major-hurdle-to-deliver-scalable-universal-fault-tolerant-quantum-computers-by-2029), [IonQ](https://www.ionq.com/news/ionq-publishes-definitive-technical-report-establishing-its-fault-tolerant-quantum-computing-trajectory---setting-a-new-standard-for-technical-specificity-and-transparency), and others—are pursuing different approaches to building fault-tolerant quantum computers. While recent advances have demonstrated logical qubits and improved error correction, no company has yet publicly deployed a fully fault-tolerant system for commercial use. Commercial quantum computing is currently available through cloud platforms, but these services provide noisy or partially error-corrected hardware rather than fully fault-tolerant machines.

Whether a fault-tolerant quantum computer will become commercially available before 2030 remains uncertain. IBM has [publicly stated that it aims to make its first large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computer available to customers in 2029](https://newsroom.ibm.com/2026-06-02-ibm-commits-more-than-10-billion-to-quantum-computing,-funding-its-roadmap-from-todays-leading-systems-to-the-worlds-first-fault-tolerant-quantum-computers), while other companies have published similar—but non-binding—roadmaps targeting the late 2020s or early 2030s.
question.resolution_criteria: The question will resolve as **Yes** if, before **January 1, 2030,** at least one organization has made **a fault-tolerant quantum computer** available to **commercial users** through a paid commercial offering (including cloud access, dedicated hardware, or managed services). The system must demonstrably employ quantum error correction to support fault-tolerant computation rather than merely error mitigation or isolated logical-qubit demonstrations.
question.fine_print: Announcements, prototypes, internal deployments, government-only access, research collaborations, beta testing without commercial availability, or systems that are only error-mitigated do not qualify.
question.short_title: Will fault-tolerant quantum computers be available commercially before 2030?
